course.title: AI in Physics Research – Generative AI & Knowledge Platforms

assessment.description: Weekly hands-on coding assignments in Weeks 1–4 covering foundational GenAI and MCP techniques applied to physics problems. Graded on methodology correctness, reproducibility, physical plausibility, and code clarity.

A written proposal (RevTeX, 2 pages) and a live pitch delivered in Week 5 defining the student’s independent research project. Graded on clarity of research question, feasibility, pitch delivery, and written quality.
Structured peer code review and reading-group participation in Weeks 10–12. Graded on depth of technical feedback, constructive tone, and discussion engagement.

A complete, reproducible codebase (GitHub repository) and an academic paper (RevTeX) submitted in Week 14. Graded on reproducibility, physical interpretation, academic writing quality, and code documentation.
A public presentation of project results delivered at a departmental showcase in Week 14. Graded on clarity of narrative, defensibility of AI claims, Q&A handling, and visual presentation.

weeks.title: GenAI Underpinnings
topics: Course overview and expectations
What is a large language model: tokens, attention, and next-token prediction
Capabilities and hard limits of current generative AI in scientific contexts
Responsible use: attribution, hallucination risk, and reproducibility expectations
Setting up a reproducible AI-assisted research environment
learning_objectives: Identify the core architectural ideas behind transformer-based LLMs and why they matter for physics researchers
Distinguish between appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI-generated outputs in scientific work
Set up a working Python environment with LLM API access and version control
milestones: Environment setup complete (Python, Jupyter, API keys, GitHub account)
Mini-assignment 1 distributed
weeks.grading_notes: Mini-assignment 1 due before first class of Week 2. Graded under Standard Curriculum Mini-Assignments (20%).

weeks.title: Vibe-Coding & Pitfalls
topics: AI-assisted coding workflows: GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT for code generation
Prompt patterns for code generation: specification-first, test-driven, iterative refinement
Common failure modes: hallucinated APIs, off-by-one errors, plausible-but-wrong physics
Detecting and documenting AI coding errors in a physics context
learning_objectives: Use an AI coding assistant to generate, debug, and refine a physics analysis script
Identify and document at least three distinct AI coding failure modes in a provided codebase
Apply a test-driven prompting strategy to improve AI code reliability
milestones: Mini-assignment 2 distributed
weeks.grading_notes: Mini-assignment 2 due before first class of Week 3. Graded under Standard Curriculum Mini-Assignments (20%).

weeks.title: RAG & Knowledge Platforms
topics: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): embeddings, vector stores, retrieval, generation
Semantic search over physics literature: arXiv, INSPIRE-HEP, NASA ADS
Building a local RAG pipeline for a physics subdomain
Evaluating retrieval quality: precision, recall, and relevance for scientific queries
learning_objectives: Implement a RAG pipeline that retrieves relevant arXiv abstracts and grounds LLM answers in the literature
Evaluate retrieval precision on a set of physics questions with known correct sources
Identify when RAG improves LLM accuracy and when it fails for scientific queries
milestones: Mini-assignment 3 distributed
weeks.grading_notes: Mini-assignment 3 due before first class of Week 4. Graded under Standard Curriculum Mini-Assignments (20%).

weeks.title: Tool Use & Agents
topics: Model Context Protocol (MCP): specification, servers, clients, and tool calling
Connecting LLMs to external scientific databases and APIs (SIMBAD, Materials Project, arXiv API)
Agentic workflows: multi-step reasoning, tool chaining, and error recovery
Safety and rate-limit considerations when integrating external APIs
learning_objectives: Build a minimal MCP server that exposes a physics database query as an LLM-callable tool
Implement a multi-step agentic workflow that retrieves data and produces a physics-relevant report
Evaluate the reliability and failure modes of a tool-augmented LLM pipeline
milestones: Mini-assignment 4 distributed
Students begin identifying potential project topics
weeks.grading_notes: Mini-assignment 4 due before first class of Week 5. Graded under Standard Curriculum Mini-Assignments (20%).

weeks.title: GenAI in Theoretical Physics
topics: Applications of generative AI to theoretical physics: symbolic computation, equation discovery, literature synthesis
LLMs as research assistants: drafting derivations, checking dimensional analysis, generating counterexamples
Formulating a falsifiable AI-assisted research question in a physics subdomain
Structuring a research proposal and delivering a live pitch
learning_objectives: Articulate a specific, feasible research question that uses GenAI or MCP as a core method
Identify the dataset, tools, and evaluation criteria for the proposed project
Deliver a clear, time-bounded oral pitch and receive peer critique
milestones: Written project proposal submitted (RevTeX, 2 pages)
Live proposal pitch delivered in class
Project approved by instructor
weeks.grading_notes: Graded under Project Proposal & Pitch (15%). Written proposal and live pitch together.

weeks.title: Building MCP Servers
topics: MCP server architecture in depth: resources, tools, prompts, and sampling
Designing MCP servers for specific physics use cases (simulation output inspection, database aggregation, unit conversion)
Authentication, error handling, and rate limiting in production MCP servers
Integrating MCP servers into student projects
learning_objectives: Design and implement a project-relevant MCP server with at least two distinct tool endpoints
Demonstrate that the MCP server is callable from an LLM client with verifiable outputs
Document the server’s tools, expected inputs, and failure modes
milestones: Students identify the primary model or method for their project
MCP server prototype demonstrated in class

weeks.title: Evaluating AI in Physics
topics: Evaluation frameworks for AI in scientific contexts: accuracy, calibration, reproducibility
Benchmarking AI outputs against physical ground truth and experimental data
Uncertainty quantification for AI-generated quantities
Critical reading of AI-in-physics papers: identifying overclaiming and undisclosed failure modes
learning_objectives: Design an evaluation protocol for an AI component in their project with explicit success criteria
Apply at least one quantitative evaluation metric to an AI-generated output and compare to a baseline
Critique an AI-in-physics paper for evaluation completeness and reproducibility
milestones: Project architecture diagram submitted
Annotated bibliography of 3 relevant papers submitted

weeks.title: Advanced Platform Integration
topics: Integrating multiple knowledge platforms into a unified AI pipeline (SIMBAD + arXiv + Materials Project)
Data wrangling and normalization across heterogeneous scientific databases
Handling API failures, partial results, and stale data in long-running agentic pipelines
Project data pipeline implementation and testing
learning_objectives: Implement the data ingestion layer of their project pipeline, integrating at least two external data sources
Handle and log at least two distinct API failure modes gracefully in their pipeline
Produce a data provenance record documenting the source and transformation of each dataset used
milestones: Project data pipeline complete and tested on real data
Initial analysis results documented in a lab notebook

weeks.title: Debugging Agentic Workflows
topics: Systematic debugging of agentic pipelines: tracing tool calls, inspecting intermediate outputs, reproducing failures
Common agentic failure modes: prompt drift, tool hallucination, infinite loops, context overflow
Logging and observability for multi-step AI pipelines
Reproducibility for agentic workflows: recording tool call sequences and random seeds
learning_objectives: Apply a structured debugging protocol to an agentic workflow with a planted failure
Add logging to their project pipeline sufficient to reproduce any failure from the logs alone
Document at least one bug found and fixed in their own project pipeline during the week
milestones: Project repository set up on GitHub with README and environment file
At least one key analysis result produced and committed to the repository

weeks.title: Ethics & Reproducibility
topics: Ethics of AI-assisted research: attribution, transparency, and disclosure of AI tool use
Reproducibility standards for AI-assisted physics papers: what must be shared and how
Structured peer code review: reading code against a physics-specific rubric
Writing actionable, constructive code review comments
learning_objectives: Apply a structured rubric to review a peer’s AI-generated analysis code with line-level comments
Write a limitations and ethics statement for their own project describing AI tool use
Identify at least one reproducibility gap in a peer’s codebase and propose a specific fix
milestones: First round of peer code reviews completed
Each student receives written feedback on their project codebase
weeks.grading_notes: Peer code review quality graded under Peer Review & Participation (15%).

weeks.title: Seminar/Reading Group Part 1
topics: Student-selected paper reading groups on project-relevant AI methods in physics
Communicating AI results to a physics audience: framing, caveats, and validation
Structuring a results section for a physics paper that uses AI methods
Responding to skeptical reviewer questions about AI methodology
learning_objectives: Lead or contribute substantively to a reading group discussion on a paper relevant to their project
Draft a results section that interprets AI outputs in physical terms with uncertainty estimates
Formulate a defensible response to a skeptical reviewer question about their AI methodology
milestones: Reading group discussions held; summaries posted to course repository
Draft results section submitted for peer comment
weeks.grading_notes: Reading group participation graded under Peer Review & Participation (15%).

weeks.title: Seminar/Reading Group Part 2
topics: Second student-led reading group session on advanced or cross-cutting AI-in-physics topics
Second round of structured peer code review with focus on reproducibility and documentation
Addressing review feedback: resolving comments and documenting decisions
Preparing code and documentation for public release
learning_objectives: Provide and receive a second round of peer review focused on reproducibility gaps and documentation completeness
Resolve all blocking code review comments and document decisions in commit messages
Write a limitations section that honestly characterizes the AI methods and their failure modes
milestones: Second round of peer code reviews completed
All blocking review comments resolved in the project repository
weeks.grading_notes: Peer code review and reading group participation graded under Peer Review & Participation (15%).

weeks.title: Scientific Communication
topics: RevTeX document structure: abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion
AI-assisted writing: using LLMs to improve clarity and concision without distorting meaning
Linking code to paper claims: ensuring every quantitative result is traceable to a notebook cell
Preparing publication-quality figures and tables
learning_objectives: Assemble a complete draft paper in RevTeX with all required sections
Use an LLM to improve prose clarity while preserving scientific accuracy
Ensure every quantitative claim in the paper is traceable to a specific code cell or figure
milestones: Complete paper draft submitted for instructor review
Final codebase tagged and repository prepared for submission

weeks.title: Showcase & Wrap-Up
topics: Final project codebase and paper submission
Departmental showcase presentations to faculty and peers
Q&A and defense of AI-assisted methodology under adversarial questioning
Course retrospective: what worked, what did not, future directions for AI in physics research
learning_objectives: Present a complete AI-assisted physics research project to a departmental audience
Defend methodological choices and AI outputs under adversarial questioning
Reflect critically on the role of AI tools in the research process
milestones: Final codebase and paper submitted (GitHub repository + PDF)
Showcase presentation delivered to departmental audience
Course retrospective discussion completed
weeks.grading_notes: Final Codebase & Paper (25%) and Departmental Showcase Presentation (25%) both due this week.
